articles.headline: Falcons' Anterio Thompson says he can't play football due to spinal cord issue
articles.description: Falcons rookie DT Anterio Thompson revealed on Instagram this week that he was told he would never play football again due to a genetic mutation of his spinal cord.
articles.headlineJa: ファルコンズのアンテリオ・トンプソン、脊髄の問題によりフットボールの継続は不可能と語る
articles.descriptionJa: ファルコンズの新人DTアンテリオ・トンプソンは今週、自身の脊髄の遺伝子変異により、二度とフットボールをプレーできないと言われたことをInstagramで明かした。
articles.body:
Atlanta Falcons rookie defensive tackle Anterio Thompson wrote this week on Instagram that he has a genetic mutation of his spinal cord and was told he would never play football again.

Thompson, who was selected in the sixth round of the 2026 draft, has been on the reserve/non-football injury list since training camp and has not been with the team since the spring. Before Thompson's post, no information about his injury had been released by either Thompson's camp or the Falcons.

When asked about Thompson on Friday, before the Instagram post circulated publicly, Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said he had no update. Technically, Thompson would be able to return this season from the reserve/non-football injury list, but now that seems moot.

Thompson and a representative did not respond to a request for comment from ESPN.

"Mentally, I've been better than anyone would be in my situation," Thompson wrote on Instagram. "I was told I would never play football again due to a genetic mutation in my spinal cord that I had no idea about."

Thompson added: "As a football player you know one day you'll have to hang up your cleats but you just hope it's on your own terms. It's hard to explain what it feels like to go through the highest of highs to the lowest of lows in the [sic] matter of seconds."

Thompson, 24, had 1.5 sacks and 2.5 tackles for a loss at the University of Washington last season.

Jeremiyah Love, RB, Cardinals (ankle): The rookie returned to practice this week and will play in Week 8. Fantasy managers should start him against a Cowboys team that allows the fifth-most rushing yards per game and eighth-most fantasy PPG to RBs.

Michael Wilson, WR, Cardinals (ribs): Wilson has been practicing each day to start the week, albeit in limited fashion. He will play in Week 8. He has struggled since Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded. However, this is a week to get him into starting lineups. The Cowboys rank top 10 in most yards, touchdowns and fantasy PPG ceded to WRs. That keeps him in play as a WR2 for fantasy purposes.

Lamar Jackson, QB, Ravens (ankle): The two-time MVP, who has missed the past three games, was a full participant at practice this week. He will play in Week 8. With Jackson suiting up, you play him in fantasy for what could be the highest-scoring game of the week.

Dalton Kincaid, TE, Bills (chest): Kincaid is questionable headed into Week 8 against the Ravens. Coming off the bye and practicing this week, he seems more likely to play than not. He could be involved with the highest-scoring game of the week, which puts Kincaid in play as a low-end E1. If he plays, use him over Mark Andrews, Tyler Higbee and other streaming options.

DJ Moore, WR, Bills (shoulder): Moore has been limited at practice but is on the right side of questionable for Week 8. If he suits up, fantasy managers should play him. He faces a Ravens defense that has allowed the third-most WR yards. When these teams matched up last season, they combined for 81 points. You want exposure to this game.

Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Bengals (ankle): Chase is dealing with a minor ankle injury but will play this weekend and be a focal part of the Bengals' offensive attack. As always, if Chase plays for the Bengals, he is a must-start in fantasy football.

articles.headline: Sources: Commanders' Daron Payne likely IR-bound after practice injury
articles.description: Commanders DT Daron Payne suffered a significant foot injury in practice Friday that likely will land him on injured reserve, sources told NFL Network.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：コマンダーズのダロン・ペイン、練習中の負傷により故障者リスト入りへ
articles.descriptionJa: コマンダーズのDTダロン・ペインは金曜日の練習中に深刻な足の負傷を負い、故障者リスト（IR）入りする可能性が高いと関係者がNFL Networkに語った。
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- Washington Commanders defensive tackle Daron Payne suffered a significant foot injury in practice Friday that likely will land him on injured reserve, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.

The injury occurred during a team drill on a day that is considered a light practice. He'll undergo more tests Saturday, but initial X-rays showed significant damage, a team source told ESPN.

Depending on what the additional tests reveal, it's possible Payne, who's in the final year of his contract, will be done for the season.

It's yet another blow for the Commanders, who are 1-4-1 in a pivotal third season for coach Dan Quinn. They also will be without their other starting defensive end, Javon Kinlaw, for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles (2-5) because of a knee injury.

Payne has been a longtime starter along Washington's defensive line since the organization drafted him with the No. 13 pick in 2018. He's their longest-tenured position player. He started every game between 2020 and 2024, missed only two games last season and has started every one this year. 

Payne made the Pro Bowl in 2022 after recording a career-best 11.5 sacks. He has had a combined 11 sacks since that season and that was the only year he topped five.

But his strength has been playing the run.

Earlier Friday, Quinn said he valued Payne's "strength inside, his power, and oftentimes that's where he wins on whether it's pass rush or [tackles for a loss]. But some of the dirty work doesn't go in a stat, but you can definitely feel it."

Washington does have depth at defensive end with Deatrich Wise Jr. and Charles Omenihu.

It also opened the 21-day window this week on defensive end Jer'Zhan Newton, who tore a pectoral muscle in a preseason game vs. the Miami Dolphins on Aug. 14. He's listed as questionable for Sunday.

articles.headline: Philadelphia 76ers star Brown to miss Friday NBA Cup game vs. New York Knicks
articles.description: Philadelphia 76ers veteran forward Jaylen Brown will be out of Friday's NBA Cup game against the New York Knicks with a left knee patella injury, the team announced.
articles.headlineJa: フィラデルフィア・76ersのスター、ブラウンが金曜日のNBAカップのニューヨーク・ニックス戦を欠場
articles.descriptionJa: フィラデルフィア・76ersは、ベテランフォワードのジェイレン・ブラウンが左膝の膝蓋骨の負傷により、金曜日のNBAカップのニューヨーク・ニックス戦を欠場すると発表した。
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA -- Sixers forward Jaylen Brown will be out of Friday's NBA Cup game against the New York Knicks with a left patella injury, the team announced.

The team reported that Brown had left knee soreness after Wednesday's win over the Pacers and then listed him as questionable for Friday's game before downgrading him to doubtful.

With Brown out, coach Nick Nurse said that the Sixers would start forward Dean Wade. When asked if Brown's injury was concerning, Nurse didn't provide much clarity.

"Well, we want him out there, right? So I just know he can't play tonight," he said. "He's out tonight, that's what I know."

Brown has been perhaps the team's best perimeter defender so far this season, while also third in points per game (20.6).

articles.headline: Sources: Mark Walter, Josh Kushner finalize all terms of $12.5B Lakers sale
articles.description: Lakers owner Mark Walter and Thrive Capital founder Josh Kushner met Thursday to finalize the transaction and are expected to sign the formal agreement soon, sources told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：マーク・ウォルターとジョシュ・クシュナー、125億ドルのレイカーズ売却に関する全条件を最終決定
articles.descriptionJa: レイカーズのオーナーであるマーク・ウォルターとThrive Capitalの創設者ジョシュ・クシュナーは木曜日に会談して取引を最終決定し、間もなく正式な合意書に署名する見込みであると関係者がESPNに語った。
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers owner Mark Walter and Thrive Capital founder Josh Kushner have agreed on all outstanding terms of the sale of the team at a $12.5 billion valuation, sources close to the negotiations told ESPN.

The two men met in person Thursday at Walter's home in Florida to finalize the transaction and are expected to sign the formal agreement soon, those sources said.

Once the agreement is signed, it will be reviewed by the NBA. That process generally takes some time as the league reviews financing and ownership structure.

Sources close to the negotiations said that Kushner has assured Walter he has raised all the money necessary to complete the sale.

Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger reached a stunning deal with Walter to buy the Lakers at the $12.5 billion valuation and have been working on the details of the transaction the past few months.

articles.headline: Inside the stunning 72-hour Lakers sale -- and the uncertainty that still looms
articles.description: Three days of secret talks resulted in Mark Walter flipping the Lakers -- and reignited yet another round of bickering among the six Buss siblings.
articles.headlineJa: レーカーズの衝撃的な72時間の売却劇――そして今なお漂う不透明感
articles.descriptionJa: 3日間にわたる極秘交渉の結果、マーク・ウォルターがレーカーズの売却を決定。これにより、バス家の6兄弟の間で再び論争が再燃している。
articles.body:
BOB IGER WAS on his 213-foot sailing superyacht on Aug. 12, winding down a monthlong vacation in Europe following a historic, two-decade run as CEO of Disney.

The biggest event of the day was supposed to be the first total solar eclipse over the continent in more than a century.

Millions of tourists, including Iger, had booked vacations along the eclipse's path from Greenland to Southern Spain during the syzygy -- a word derived from Ancient Greek for "yoked together" -- which describes a rare astronomical event in which three or more celestial bodies align in a straight line.

During a solar eclipse, the moon sits exactly between the sun and Earth, casting its shadow onto Earth. Some enjoy the rare view -- through special sunglasses.

Others ascribe great meaning and magic to eclipses. As those tourists headed to viewing spots for the solar eclipse across Europe, Iger was in a wholly different syzygy with his longtime friend and business partner Josh Kushner and Los Angeles Lakers owner Mark Walter.

The alignment of three financial heavy hitters was about to turn what should have been a once-in-a-generation event -- last year's record-breaking sale of the Lakers from the Buss family to Walter -- into the NBA's most shocking news -- again.

Instead of getting into position to watch the solar eclipse, Iger was furiously working the phones from Italy to consummate a stunning event of his own -- a $12.5 billion sale of the Lakers seemingly out of nowhere, creating an eclipse unto itself across the worlds of sports and business.

Little did anyone know that these secret, cross-continental talks were about to put the Lakers in significant transition yet again -- with new owners evaluating everything and everyone; squabbling former owners again jostling for power and money; and an overhauled roster finally built in the image of its superstar, Luka Doncic.

Interviews with more than a dozen team insiders, league executives and others with intimate knowledge of the sale reveal how the deal, which was made over a furious 72 hours, upstaged an already-transformative offseason -- and reignited yet another unresolved round of messy public bickering among the six Buss siblings that still hangs uncomfortably over the beginning of this new season.

JUST A YEAR ago, Lakers governor Jeanie Buss had shocked the sports world by negotiating a sale to Walter after 46 years of family ownership. Though that deal was eventually approved by all six siblings, it was not a clean process.

According to several family sources, younger brothers Joey and Jesse Buss -- who, because of a "last-man standing" provision in Dr. Jerry Buss's family trust, were positioned to run the team one day after their older siblings died -- hadn't responded to the vote when the sale was initially announced.

articles.headline: Michael Carrick: 'Hard truths' have been shared amid Man United slump
articles.description: Manchester United manager Michael Carrick said "hard truths" have been spoken between himself, the players and the club hierarchy amid an eight-game winless run.
articles.headlineJa: マイケル・キャリック：「マンUの低迷の中、『厳しい真実』が語られた」
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのマイケル・キャリック監督は、8試合未勝利が続く中で、自身と選手、そしてクラブ幹部の間で「厳しい真実」が共有されたと語った。
articles.body:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has said "hard truths" have been spoken between himself, the players and the club hierarchy during an eight-game winless run that has left him fighting for his job at Old Trafford.

United face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday aiming to win a domestic fixture for the first time since a 5-2 Premier League victory against Ipswich on Aug. 30 -- United's only league win so far this season.

- Tielemans backs Carrick to stay in Man United job

- Global power ranking: The top 20 soccer teams in the world, ranked!

- Carrick: 'Fully committed' Fernandes retains Man United captaincy

Last Sunday's 3-0 home defeat against Bournemouth, four days after a humiliating 4-1 Champions League loss away to Italian debutants Como, raised serious doubts over Carrick's United future before the 45-year-old was told by senior figures that he would remain in charge with pressure mounting to halt the dismal run of form.

But with criticism directed at his players and also CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox following their failure to sufficiently bolster the United squad this summer, Carrick said blunt conversations have taken place between parties in an effort to resolve the team's problems.

"It's pretty clear," Carrick told reporters. "It's not always rosy and nice conversations between anyone, whether that's between me and the players or whether it's between me, Jason, Omar or the owners.

"It's the truth, it's the hard truth at times and it's what we need to move forward. Whatever we need to move forward, we'll do.

"We always do what we think is going to get the best out of the team. Whether that's certain players that, of course, you speak to at certain points, that's normal.

"That's why, if you ask for leaders in the dressing room, you want opinions on certain things and there's going to be times when you ask that, that's fine.

"Absolutely no problem. It doesn't mean that we always agree with that, but absolutely no problem with that. And then we head off in the same direction."

United are in their worst run of form since the 1988-89 season and have made their worst start to a league campaign since 1986-87, when manager Ron Atkinson was fired and replaced by Alex Ferguson.

But Carrick said that much of the team's issues are rooted in a loss of confidence -- something he says can be rectified.

"Confidence is the beauty of sport," he said. "Confidence is in some ways the major factor of that belief, that self-belief, that confidence level.

"It kind of trumps everything else in terms of level of performance. But the beauty about confidence, it can come back quickly in one moment, one thing in a game, one win, one result.

"We've seen it before, we've seen it a few months ago, it can come back quickly. And that's what keeps you pushing and keeps you believing that it's always that close and what's possible is always within touching distance.

articles.headline: Achraf Hakimi scores 1st career hat trick as Luis Enrique makes PSG history
articles.description: Right back Achraf Hakimi claimed a first career hat trick and provided two assists as Luis Enrique became the winningest coach in Paris Saint-Germain history on Friday.
articles.headlineJa: アシュラフ・ハキミがキャリア初のハットトリック、ルイス・エンリケがPSGの歴史を塗り替える
articles.descriptionJa: 金曜日、右サイドバックのアシュラフ・ハキミがキャリア初のハットトリックを達成し、2アシストを記録。ルイス・エンリケはパリ・サンジェルマン史上最多勝利を記録する監督となった。
articles.body:
Right back Achraf Hakimi claimed a first career hat trick and provided two assists as Luis Enrique became the winningest coach in Paris Saint-Germain history on Friday.

The Ligue 1 leaders came from behind to thrash bottom club Le Havre 5-1 with Morocco international Hakimi playing a role in all five goals.

- PSG's Luis Enrique: Vitinha's Ballon d'Or ranking too low

- PSG star Kvaratskhelia undergoes successful knee surgery

He is just the fourth player with five goal contributions in a single game in the last four seasons in the top five European leagues. The last player to achieve that feat in France's Ligue 1 was Neymar for PSG in August 2022.

The result took Luis Enrique to 127 wins, breaking a tie with Laurent Blanc for most in PSG's history.

The reigning French and European champions briefly looked in danger of suffering a major shock when former Sunderland and West Brom forward Josh Maja gave the winless hosts an 18th-minute lead.

But captain Hakimi set up Mika Godts to level before completing the turnaround with a smart finish two minutes later and then curling home a fine 20-yard free kick early in the second half.

Hakimi, who had not scored this season ahead of kickoff, completed his landmark treble in fortuitous fashion in the 69th minute, after his through ball allowed Senny Mayulu to register the visitors' fourth goal.

The 27-year-old's first hat trick for club and country came in the 486th game of his career.

PSG's victory was their ninth in a row in all competitions -- and sixth successive league win -- after they picked up just a point from their opening three fixtures.

In the continued absence of key attackers Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia through injury, Luis Enrique made five changes to his starting XI following Monday's 2-0 success over Lyon.

Information from ESPN Research and PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Colts' Shane Steichen: WR Josh Downs 'ready to go' despite trade request
articles.description: Colts coach Shane Steichen says receiver Josh Downs practiced all week and is "ready to go" despite the trade request he made earlier this week.
articles.headlineJa: コルツのシェーン・ステイケン：「トレードを要求したものの、WRジョシュ・ダウンズは『準備ができている』」
articles.descriptionJa: コルツのシェーン・ステイケン監督は、ワイドレシーバーのジョシュ・ダウンズが今週初めにトレードを要求したものの、一週間練習に取り組んでおり「準備はできている」と述べた。
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Colts receiver Josh Downs will perform his normal role Sunday against the host Jacksonville Jaguars despite his trade request this week, coach Shane Steichen said.

Downs requested a trade earlier this week amid the Colts' organizational changes. General manager Chris Ballard was fired Oct. 19, and cornerstone players Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded this week to the Seahawks and 49ers, respectively.

Downs seemed frustrated when he spoke to reporters Wednesday, saying when asked about whether he wanted to remain in Indianapolis, "I'm here right now. I'm where my feet are. We've got the Jags this weekend, and so I'm in the game plan. So I've got to be ready to go."

Steichen said he had a discussion with Downs in recent days and implored him to remain focused on the present.

"'Hey, you're a professional'," Steichen said, recounting the conversation. "'Obviously, you requested a trade. But you're on this football team, and you've got to show up. We've got to go play a game on Sunday.'"

As for how Downs performed during the week's practices, Steichen said, "He's a pro. He practiced this week. He's ready to go. We're expecting for him to be his best on Sunday."

Downs has a team-high 307 receiving yards this season as he's been asked to do more in the absence of No. 1 receiver Alec Pierce. The Colts have also been missing top tight end Tyler Warren in their past two games, further impacting the passing game.

It has all led to increased attention from defenses for Downs, who has seen mixed results and has a career-low catch rate of 56.5%.

Downs is in the final year of his rookie contract. Sources told ESPN that teams have inquired about Downs' availability, but it remains unclear whether Indianapolis is willing to deal him.

"I'm open to whatever," Downs said this week. "Whatever comes my way, comes my way."

articles.headline: Ja Morant out at least 4 weeks with hamstring strain suffered against Grizzlies
articles.description: Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant sustained a left hamstring strain in his first game against the Grizzlies, his former team, and will be out at least four weeks.
articles.headlineJa: ジャ・モラント、グリズリーズ戦でのハムストリング損傷により少なくとも4週間の離脱
articles.descriptionJa: トレイルブレイザーズのガード、ジャ・モラントは、古巣グリズリーズとの初戦で左ハムストリングの損傷を負い、少なくとも4週間は戦列を離れる見込みだ。
articles.body:
Portland Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant has sustained a Grade 2 left hamstring strain and will be out at least four weeks before being reevaluated, the team announced Friday.

Morant suffered the injury while playing in his first game against his former team, the Memphis Grizzlies, on Thursday night. He exited in the fourth quarter and did not return.

Coach Micah Nori said postgame that Morant felt a twinge in his hamstring before leaving the game.

The setback comes amid a promising start for Morant and the Trail Blazers, who are 3-1 entering Friday. The four-week timeline means that Morant will miss at least the next 15 games. The Trail Blazers begin a four-game road trip against the Utah Jazz on Saturday.

Morant, who was acquired by Portland in a surprising offseason trade, has joined Damian Lillard in a star-studded backcourt that has delivered the NBA's No. 3 offense through Thursday. Morant, a two-time All-Star, scored a season-high 23 points in a victory over the Los Angeles Lakers on Tuesday. He has averaged 15.8 points and 5.5 assists over his first four games with the Trail Blazers.

In Morant's absence, Nori will likely lean more heavily on backup guards Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. The first-year coach said earlier this week that he had sought to limit minutes for both Lillard and Morant to take advantage of his backcourt depth.

Morant, 27, has dealt with a series of injuries in recent seasons, and he played in just 20 games in 2025-26 due to an elbow sprain.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Source: Fever hires Blazers' Sheri Sam as assistant GM
articles.description: Sheri Sam, who was the scouting manager for the Trail Blazers, has been hired as assistant general manager of the WNBA's Fever, a source told ESPN.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者によると、フィーバーがブレイザーズのシェリ・サムをアシスタントGMに採用
articles.descriptionJa: トレイルブレイザーズのスキャウティングマネージャーを務めていたシェリ・サムが、WNBAのフィーバーのアシスタントGMに採用されたと関係者がESPNに語った。
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever have hired Sheri Sam as assistant general manager, a source confirmed to ESPN on Friday.

Sam joins the Fever from the Portland Trail Blazers, where she had held the position of scouting manager since 2022. She played 10 years in the WNBA and won championships in Seattle (2004) and Detroit (2008).

Her responsibilities with the Trail Blazers included collegiate and professional player scouting and evaluation. The Fever had planned to invest in their scouting and analytics efforts, and the addition of Sam was one step in that direction.

Indiana remains without a team president and general manager after Kelly Krauskopf stepped down and Amber Cox was fired last week.

The Fever lost to the Las Vegas Aces in the first round of the playoffs after finishing with a 28-16 regular-season record and earning the No. 6 seed for the third consecutive season.

Sam's hiring was first reported by the Indy Star.

articles.headline: Bayern Munich not allowing Kompany to be involved in Dortmund clash
articles.description: Vincent Kompany won't be on the sidelines for Bayern's match against Borussia Dortmund following his hospitalization last week.
articles.body:
MUNICH -- Bayern Munich are not allowing coach Vincent Kompany to be part of their plans for Saturday's Klassiker against Bundesliga rival Borussia Dortmund following his collapse and hospitalization last week.

Assistant coach Aaron Danks said on Friday there were orders not to discuss the game with Kompany, even though he's out of hospital and recovering at home.

"We don't talk to him about football. We've been given clear instructions there," Danks said. "He needs to recover and spend time with his family. We're not getting him involved so he can be fully back at it when he returns."

Danks oversaw a 6-1 win over Magdeburg in the German Cup on Wednesday. Saturday's game against Dortmund is likely to see Harry Kane return to action after winning the Ballon d'Or on Monday.

Danks said not much has changed in how Bayern are training for the game, adding that Kompany's assistants aren't "mini-Vinnies" but have skill sets which complement each other to work together in his absence.

Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl told German broadcaster ARD on Wednesday that Kompany was treated for meningeal irritation, which is an inflammation of the tissue around the brain or spinal cord.

Before his collapse, Kompany had also been struggling with a viral infection and a hip injury.

The New York Knicks are planning to decline Pacome Dadiet's fourth-year option worth $5.37 million, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The decision will make Dadiet an unrestricted free agent next summer.

How Dybantsa will impact the Wizards on the court

After missing the first four games of the season with an ankle injury, No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa will make his regular-season debut Wednesday, ESPN's Shams Charania reported.

Dybantsa's arrival could give the Wizards one of the best starting lineups in the Eastern Conference -- which would be quite a change of pace for a team that hasn't won 20 games in a season since 2022-23. Anthony Davis has been explosive and productive through four games. Trae Young is averaging 22 points and a league-best 11 assists per game. And Kyshawn George is up to 18 PPG as he continues to make strides as an all-around NBA contributor. Add Dybantsa to that mix and there's legitimate reason for excitement in Washington.

The only downside is that Dybantsa should command plenty of playing time, which could further squeeze an overcrowded Wizards rotation. Already, 2025 first-rounder Will Riley has seen his playing time crater, but he, Tre Johnson and Bilal Coulibaly are all wings who will now likely come off the bench, yet deserve the opportunity to continue their development. -- Zach Kram

articles.headline: USMNT star Christian Pulisic signs new AC Milan contract through 2031
articles.description: United States star Christian Pulisic has signed a new contract with AC Milan through 2031.
articles.body:
United States star Christian Pulisic has signed a new contract with AC Milan through 2031.

The deal for Pulisic, 28, was reported by ESPN on Wednesday and confirmed on Friday, a day after AC Milan announced plans for their new stadium.

"Captain America's Rossonero mission continues," wrote AC Milan on Friday.

Pulisic's deal was due to expire in June 2027, but he has committed his future to the Rossoneri on a contract that will take him beyond the next World Cup.

"There's a lot of emotions, I'm really proud to re-sign here in Milan because I'm really just in love with this team, this club, everything about it," Pulisic said in an interview on the club's social media pages. "The feeling that I got, the support from the fans through all of the good and bad times, I knew immediately that this was the place for me.:

He joined AC Milan in 2023 from Chelsea for a fee in the region of €22 million ($24.4m). At the Serie A club, Pulisic has 44 goals and 28 assists across his 141 appearances and was the club's top scorer in the 2024-25 season.

"Milan has given me everything, it feels like home for me," he said. "It's where I want to spend my next years because I'm just really happy here, I love it here, my family loves it here. I want to continue to give everything and bring this club to the top.

He added: "I look at my whole life as a book, to be honest, and i feel like this is the most important chapter right now."

Pulisic signed for Borussia Dortmund back in 2015 and established himself as one of the best young players in the Bundesliga. Chelsea signed him for £58m ($71.7m) in 2018, and he won the 2021 Champions League there.

But injury disrupted his progress at Chelsea, and in 2023, AC Milan saw off competition from Juventus, Lyon and Galatasaray to sign him.

- Pulisic staying in Milan reflects his club career: Good, but not quite great

- Cavan Sullivan turned 17 last month, but he's already playing like an MLS MVP

- Ex-USMNT star Eddie Johnson to train 3-year-old removed from Florida soccer game

Pulisic missed most of AC Milan's preseason due to the injury he sustained during the World Cup. But after a steady reintegration into the first team under Ruben Amorim, he has become an integral part of the manager's Milan blueprint, playing in the No. 10 role and on the wing.

Pulisic's new deal follows the unveiling of AC Milan's new stadium, which will be ready in 2031. The clubs said in a news release Thursday that the deal represented "one of the largest stadium naming rights agreements in global sport."

At the international level, Pulisic has established himself as a key player for the USMNT with 33 goals in 90 appearances. He played in the 2022 and 2026 World Cups for the USMNT and won U.S. Soccer Male Player of the Year in 2017, 2019, 2021 and 2023.
